# local 0008: Arithmetic on the address of an element of a nested array of function pointers steps by a row

- Category: [Fixes](../../fix.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17193
- Recommended action: Apply the patch.
- Patch: [local-0008.patch](../../patches/local-0008.patch), commit [`ee1c45cd2`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/ee1c45cd2e40862c9a53a34aafb332ae5da3c342). Applies to r17193 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

When an array of function pointers is an array element, a struct member, or the target of a
pointer, the address of one of its elements has the type pointer to that array. Arithmetic on the
address and indexing through it step by the size of the array. The file below was compiled on
r17176 with `sdcc -mmcs51 p2.c` and run in ucsim.

```c
void (*fp[2][2]) (void);
unsigned char guard[2];

__xdata __at (0x7000) unsigned char res[5];

void h (void) { }
void set (void) { (&fp[1][0])[1] = h; }
int diff (void) { return &fp[1][1] - &fp[0][1]; }

void main (void)
{
  set ();
  res[0] = (fp[1][1] == h);
  res[1] = (&fp[1][0] + 1 == &fp[1][1]);
  res[2] = diff ();
  res[3] = guard[0];
  res[4] = guard[1];
  for (;;);
}
```

After the run `res` holds `00 00 01 a9 00`, and `01 01 02 00 00` is expected. `set` writes to
`_fp + 8`, and the element `fp[1][1]` is at `_fp + 6`. `_fp + 8` is the first byte after the
array, where the linker placed `guard`, and `a9 00` is the address of `h`. `diff` returns 1.

The result is `00 00 01 a9 00` with `--model-medium`, `--model-large`, `--stack-auto`, and
`--model-large --stack-auto` too. With `--model-huge`, where a function pointer has 3 bytes,
`&fp[1][0] + 1` is compiled to `_fp + 12`, and `_fp + 9` is expected. Compiled with `-mstm8 -c`
and with `-mz80 -c`, the statement in `set` also writes to `_fp + 8`. For
`struct s { char c; void (*m[2]) (void); } st;`, `(&st.m[0])[1] = h` writes to `_st + 5`, where
`_st + 3` is expected. The code for the variable `void (*fp1[4]) (void);` is correct.

The expression `(&fp[i][0])[j]` has the type of the array as well. A read of it gives the address
of the element, a call through it goes to that address, and the comparison
`(&fp[i][0])[j] == h` gets error 78 for incompatible types.

## Cause

For these arrays, `geniCodeArray` in `src/SDCCicode.c` gives the operand for an element the type
of the array and marks it with `aggr2ptr`. The condition is
`IS_ARRAY (ltype) && IS_FUNCPTR (ltype->next)`, which r9456 added with the fix for bug #2455.
`geniCodeRValue` and `geniCodeCall` read the element through an operand of that type.
`geniCodeAddressOf` makes a pointer to the type of the operand, so `&fp[i][j]` is a pointer to the
array. In the iCode for `&fp[i][0] + j`, `j` is shifted left by 2, and an element has 2 bytes.

## Fix

`geniCodeAddressOf` makes a pointer to the element type when its operand is an iTemp that has
`aggr2ptr` set and an array type, which is the operand that `geniCodeArray` makes for these
elements. The operands of `&st.m` and `&fp[i]` do not have `aggr2ptr` set, and these expressions
stay pointers to the array. `geniCodeArray`, `geniCodeRValue`, and `geniCodeCall` are unchanged.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/funptr-array-address.c` has 17 assertions for stores, arithmetic,
differences, reads, and calls through such addresses. On r17192 with the earlier patches of the
series, the three comparisons in its function `testLoad` get error 78, and the test does not
compile. This was tried for the small and large models, each with and without `--stack-auto`. A
copy without the reads and the calls, compiled by r17192, fails all 13 assertions on each of the
six mcs51 variants: the small, medium, large, and huge models, and `--stack-auto` with the small
and large models. With the patch the test passes on these six, on host, on stm8, and on ucz80.

A file of 39 functions was compiled by r17192 and with the patch for mcs51 with four sets of
options, for stm8, and for z80. The code of 20 functions differs for each of the six, and with the
patch each uses the size of the element. On mcs51 one more function differs. It converts
`&fp[i][j]` to a generic pointer, and the high byte of the address is the constant 0 with the
patch, where r17192 computes it with `addc`. The code of the 18 other functions is unchanged.
Among them are `&fp[i] + 1`, `&st.m + 1`, `fp[i][j] ()`, and the one-dimensional array.

For mcs51-small, every other regression test has the code size that it has without the patch.
With the patch series of this report up to the patch for local 0001 applied to r17192, the
regression suite ran without a failure for the nine targets above. The diagnostics suite ran
without a failure for mcs51, mcs51-large, mcs51-stack-auto, z80, and stm8.

## Related

- Bug #2691 concerns `&a[i][j]` for nested arrays of object pointers. Its patch adds a condition
  to the branch of `geniCodeAddressOf` for operands of pointer type. The operands here have an
  array type, so that patch does not change this defect, which was found with its test cases.
- The operand that `geniCodeAddressOf` returns keeps `aggr2ptr` set, as it does for elements of
  other types. `cseBBlock` in `src/SDCCcse.c` changes the type of operands with that flag when
  they are the pointer of a read or a store. A case in which this gives wrong code was not found.
